newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC says Agros premium justified.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says Agros premium justified.

text.p: HSBC James Capel in London has said its group 1998 price-earnings ratio forecast for Polish food trader and producer Agros SA of 10.5 compared to the market's 9.1 is justified by the sector's future growth.

"This premium is easily justified by the management's track record and the prospects for further development of the core business," the report dated February 24 said, when Agros was at 84 zlotys. The stock closed at 83.5 zlotys on Thursday.
HSBC saw Agros buoyed by future growth in food processing, which accounts for six percent of Polish GDP and has grown by 10 percent annually over the past four years.

It said Agros had successfully made the transition from state trading monopoly to competitive producer and that earnings quality would improve and margins rise as the firm increased moving toward production from trading.
HSBC said Agros' "ambitious but coherent" investment programme for this year and next would significantly enhance earnings over that period.
It saw the firm's current consolidated p/e ratio of 14.7 rising to 15.5 times this year's forecast earnings before dropping to the 10.5 predicted for 1998 and 7.3 in 1999.
Group earnings are seen at at 57 million zlotys in 1997, 80 million in 1998 and 110 million in 1999 on sales of 1.46 billion, 1.87 billion and 2.3 billion zlotys zlotys respectively.
